title: Lightroom's Denoise on the denoise benchmark
note: Fourteen photos get Denoise at its default Amount; six noise-free references (names ending in -clean) get nothing, so Lightroom's Denoise can be scored against Lightroom's own render of the truth (INF-14, DN-17). Thirteen are synthetic DNGs from research/benchmarks/denoise.json, seven are CC0 raws from raw.pixls.us at ISO 3200 to 20000. Exports made on the Mac can also be filed with `redlamp task add <folder> <files…>`.

steps.title: Share the 20 photos to Lightroom
steps.detail: Thirteen are synthetic test DNGs and seven are real high-ISO raws. They sync to Lightroom on your Mac.

steps.title: Open them in Lightroom on your Mac
steps.detail: Denoise isn't in Lightroom for iPhone. Use Lightroom on your Mac (or an iPad), where the photos arrive by sync.

steps.title: Leave the six -clean photos as they are
steps.detail: Photos whose names end in -clean are the noise-free references. Don't turn on Denoise or change anything on them.

steps.title: Select the other 14 photos
steps.detail: Every photo whose name doesn't end in -clean: seven synthetic DNGs and the seven raws.

steps.title: Denoise them at the default Amount
steps.detail: In the Detail panel, turn on Denoise and leave Amount at its default (50). Change nothing else. Apply it to all 14 selected photos and wait until each shows its result.

steps.title: Export all 20
steps.detail: TIF, 16 bits per component, ProPhoto RGB if Lightroom offers it (otherwise sRGB). Full size, no output sharpening, and keep the original file names.

steps.title: Share the exports back
steps.detail: Share the 20 TIFs to Redlamp Bench. They pair with their photos by file name.
